patients.summary: 36-year-old international logistics consultant with remote injection drug use in remission and a resolved hepatitis at 24 that later serology shows was hepatitis B. Healthy through routine care until acute hepatitis A after a 2026 work trip to Southeast Asia, which resolved by August.

documents.body: Hi, I'm booked as a new patient on the 21st at 9:00. I signed the release for my old doctor's office through the link you sent. Do I need to come in fasting for that first visit? I don't take any medications. Thanks, Austin

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31 y/o man here to establish care. Previously followed at another primary care office; release signed, records requested. No complaints today.

PMH:
- Injection drug use in the past, in remission. He says this is well behind him and he has not used in years; prefers not to go into specifics and I did not press. No treatment program or medication needed currently. No other substance use.
- Hepatitis at about age 24 (around 2014). Got sick after a trip overseas and was told it was "hepatitis"; no antiviral medication, no hospital stay that he recalls, and he recovered completely. Type not known to him. No records from that time.
No surgeries. Never had a blood transfusion.

Meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.

Family hx: father with alcohol use disorder. Mother has high blood pressure.

Social: single, lives by himself in Greenfield. Works as an international logistics consultant, which means stretches of travel abroad for clients. Never smoked. Drinks socially, a drink or two a week. AUDIT-C 2. PHQ-2 0.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well-appearing. Sclerae anicteric. Oropharynx clear, good dentition. Neck supple, no adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin: no rash, no track marks. Extremities without edema. Neuro grossly intact. Mood and affect appropriate.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance, new patient. CMP, CBC, lipids. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening done today given history. Tdap today (last tetanus unknown). Flu shot today. COVID primary series this spring pulled from the state registry and entered.
2. History of injection drug use, in remission. Supportive conversation; he knows he can bring it up any time.
3. Remote hepatitis, resolved by history. Will look for anything in the old records.
RTC for a physical in about a year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Austin, your bloodwork from Tuesday came back normal. Kidney and liver function, blood counts and cholesterol are all fine. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, so those don't need repeating unless something changes. Nice to have you with the practice.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Received by fax, 9 pages, in response to our request of 9/14. Covers office visits from 2019 to early 2021 only; the cover sheet says older charts were archived and are not included.

Summary of contents: two routine physicals (2019 and 2020) with normal exams and normal vitals. Problem list carries "hx IVDU, in remission" and "hx hepatitis, resolved" with no further detail or labs. No medications on file. Allergies: NKDA. A basic metabolic panel and lipid panel from 2019, both within normal limits. Immunization page lists a tetanus booster with no date. No hospital or specialist records.

Nothing here changes our history. Scanned to chart.

Reviewed by PCP 10/28.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feels well. Busy year with work, several trips abroad, no illnesses while away. Sleeping fine, exercising a few times a week (runs, some lifting).

No IV or other drug use; remains in remission. Alcohol unchanged, a drink or two on weekends. Never smoker. PHQ-2 0.

Meds none. NKDA. No change to family history.

ROS negative.

Exam: BP and vitals per flowsheet, normal. Weight stable. HEENT unremarkable, sclerae white. Neck without nodes. Cor RRR. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, no organomegaly. Skin clear. No edema.

Plan: CMP and lipids. Flu vaccine given today. Bivalent COVID booster recommended; he will come back for it after his next trip. Prior office records reviewed last fall, nothing outstanding.
See in a year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Austin, labs from your physical look good: normal kidney and liver numbers, normal sugar, and cholesterol in a healthy range. No action needed.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt in for bivalent COVID booster, Pfizer 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. Screened: no fever today, no prior reaction to vaccines, no allergies. Tolerated well, waited 15 min without issue. VIS given. Back from a work trip last week, feels fine.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid and 2023-24 COVID vaccine 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. Afebrile by report, no prior vaccine reactions, NKDA. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. VIS provided for both. Reminded him his physical is booked for 11/9.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Austin, we missed you for your physical yesterday morning. Please call or reply here and we can find a new time. The doctor has openings in December and January.

documents.title: Vaccine record for work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. One of our clients wants a copy of my vaccination record on file before I'm allowed on their warehouse floor. Can you send me whatever you have? A PDF here is fine. Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Vaccine record for work
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Austin, your immunization record is attached as a PDF (Tdap 2021, flu 2021 to 2023, COVID 2021 to 2023). Let us know if the client needs it on a specific form and we can fill that out too.

documents.title: Physical overdue
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Austin, our records show you're due for a physical (last one October 2022). Reply here or call and we'll get you on the schedule.

documents.title: RE: Physical overdue
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry, I lost track of time with travel. I'm home through the holidays. Anything the week of the 30th works, early is better.

documents.title: RE: Physical overdue
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Monday 12/30 at 8:00. You'll probably have labs, so come a few minutes early.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for a routine checkup, first in two years (missed the 2023 visit; travel). No symptoms at all. Energy good, weight steady, no GI complaints, no jaundice ever since the episode at 24.

Hx reviewed with him:
- Injection drug use in the past, in remission. Confirms no IV drug use now.
- Hepatitis about ten years ago after a trip abroad, never treated, got completely better. Still doesn't know which kind.
- Has never received blood products.
Meds: none. NKDA.
FHx: father, alcohol use disorder; mother, hypertension. Unchanged.
Social: still consulting in international logistics, on the road abroad several times a year. Never smoker. 1 to 2 drinks a week. PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

ROS: 12-point negative.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, normal BP. NAD. Sclerae anicteric. TMs and pharynx normal. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge not palpable, no splenomegaly. Skin without rash or stigmata of liver disease. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Assessment/plan:
- Routine adult exam. CMP, CBC, lipids.
- Hepatitis B: adults are now screened once regardless of risk, and with his history it is worth knowing his status. Sending surface antigen, surface antibody and core antibody, with e antigen and e antibody.
- Flu vaccine today (missed it in the fall).
- History of injection drug use, remains in remission.
One year.

documents.title: Hepatitis B and routine labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Austin, your routine labs (kidney, liver, blood counts, cholesterol) are all normal.

The hepatitis B tests show that you had hepatitis B at some point in the past and your body cleared it. The surface antigen is negative, which means there is no active or chronic infection. The core antibody is positive, which is the footprint of an old infection, and the surface antibody is positive, which means you are immune now. The e antigen is negative and e antibody positive, which fits with a cleared infection too.

This most likely explains the hepatitis you had at 24. Nothing needs treatment, you don't need the hepatitis B vaccine, and you can't pass it on.

documents.title: RE: Hepatitis B and routine labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks for explaining. Just so I'm clear, this isn't something I need to tell people about or get checked on every year?

documents.title: RE: Hepatitis B and routine labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Correct. It's a past infection that's gone, not a current one. No yearly testing, no precautions with partners or anyone else. If a blood bank or a doctor ever asks, "had hepatitis B in the past, resolved" is the accurate answer.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, lot in MAR. Feeling well, no fever, no egg or vaccine reactions in the past. 15 min observation unremarkable. Offered this season's COVID vaccine, he declined for now; will think about it. Physical scheduled 12/11.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Doing well. Travel schedule heavy again this year; feels healthy, no complaints. Got his flu shot here in October; still not interested in the COVID booster.

Remains in remission from injection drug use, no use of any kind. Social drinker, unchanged. Never smoker. PHQ-2 negative.

PMH reviewed: remote IVDU in remission; resolved hepatitis at 24, which last year's serology showed was hepatitis B, cleared and immune. No meds. NKDA. FHx unchanged.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals normal (flowsheet). Well-appearing. Anicteric. Neck: no LAD. CV: regular, no murmur. Resp: clear. Abd: soft, nontender, nondistended, no HSM. Ext: warm, no edema. Skin: no lesions of concern.

A/P: healthy 35 y/o. CMP and lipids. Nothing else due. Back in a year.

reports.text:
Indication: jaundice, right upper quadrant tenderness, elevated transaminases.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the right upper quadrant.
Liver: normal in size and echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion.
Biliary: no intrahepatic or extrahepatic ductal dilatation. Common bile duct 3 mm.
Gallbladder: normally distended, no stones, no wall thickening, no pericholecystic fluid. Sonographic Murphy sign negative.
Portal vein: patent with normal hepatopetal flow.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable.
Right kidney: normal size, no hydronephrosis.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal right upper quadrant ultrasound. No biliary obstruction.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital, Emergency Department. Date of visit 06/19/2026, arrived 18:50, discharged 23:40. Faxed to primary care 07/10/2026 on request.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: feeling unwell x1 week, urine dark.

HPI: 35M, generally healthy, about a week of malaise and tiredness. Noticed his urine turning dark, "like tea," over the same week. Some mild nausea, has not vomited. Denies abdominal pain. No fever he has measured. Got back from a work trip to Southeast Asia earlier this month. History of remote IV drug use, none currently. Had hepatitis at 24 which resolved on its own. No acetaminophen beyond a couple of doses, no supplements or herbal products, no new medications.

PMH: IVDU, in remission. Hepatitis age 24, resolved.
MEDS: none.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
FAMILY HX: father with alcohol use disorder; mother with HTN.
SOCIAL: never smoker. EtOH socially, 1 to 2 per week. International logistics consultant.

ROS: positive as in HPI. Negative for chest pain, SOB, confusion, bleeding or bruising, rash.

EXAM: T 37.3, HR 88, BP 128/78, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA.
Gen: tired-appearing, nontoxic, alert and oriented.
Eyes: sclerae mildly icteric.
CV: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nondistended, tender to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Liver not enlarged. No splenomegaly. No ascites.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae, no spider angiomata.
Neuro: nonfocal, no asterixis.

RESULTS:
AST 980 U/L, ALT 1150 U/L, total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, alk phos 110 U/L, albumin 4.2 g/dL. INR 1.0. Remainder of CMP and CBC unremarkable.
RUQ US: normal liver, no biliary dilatation, gallbladder normal.
Acute hepatitis panel sent, pending at discharge.

MDM: marked hepatocellular transaminase elevation with mild hyperbilirubinemia, preserved synthetic function (normal INR and albumin), normal mental status, imaging without obstruction. Picture is acute hepatitis, most likely viral given recent travel. Tolerating PO. No indication for admission.

DIAGNOSIS: acute hepatitis, likely viral.

DISPOSITION: home. Avoid alcohol. Limit acetaminophen. Hydrate. Follow up with PCP in 2 to 3 days for repeat labs and serology results. Return for confusion, vomiting and unable to keep fluids down, bleeding, worsening yellowing or abdominal pain.

Electronically signed, ED attending physician.
